subject: Civil Engineering
title: Commissioning: Making It Work
description: A micro-lesson that makes Commissioning: Making It Work usable.

hook.text: The building is finished — but does every system actually work? Commissioning finds out.

buildup.text: Commissioning tests every mechanical, electrical, and plumbing system under real conditions.

discovery.text: HVAC systems are balanced — airflow in every room is measured and adjusted to design specs.

twist.text: Integrated systems testing runs everything together — fire alarm, sprinklers, elevators, and power.

climax.text: Without commissioning, 15-30% of energy is wasted — systems running incorrectly from day one.

punchline.text: Building it is half the job. Making it work as designed is the other half.

quiz.question: Why is building commissioning critical before occupancy?
options: It's a legal requirement to test the building's paint color accuracy
It verifies all systems work correctly together, preventing 15-30% energy waste
It tests whether the building can withstand a category 5 hurricane

details.summary: Commissioning is the systematic process of verifying that all building systems perform as designed before handover to the owner. It includes testing mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, and control systems through functional performance tests that simulate real operating conditions.
details.whyItMatters: Without commissioning, buildings are handed over with deficient systems that waste energy, fail to maintain comfort, and require expensive troubleshooting. Commissioning ensures the owner receives a functioning facility.
takeaways: Commissioning verifies systems perform as designed under actual operating loads
It identifies installation errors and control sequence problems before occupancy
Enhanced commissioning starts during design and continues through first year

faq.question: What is the difference between commissioning and testing and balancing?
faq.answer: Testing and balancing adjusts airflow and water flow rates to match design values. Commissioning goes further by verifying that entire systems function correctly under all operating modes including heating, cooling, occupied, unoccupied, and emergency.

faq.question: When should commissioning begin on a construction project?
faq.answer: Best practice starts commissioning during design by reviewing specifications for testability. During construction, point-to-point verification checks wiring and controls as systems are installed. Functional testing begins after systems are substantially complete.
